title: Optimize / Evals 1:1 prep notes - 2026-03-12
content:
Purpose: quick 1:1 prep before sync with Aisha. Focus on the recent quality regression observed in nightly evals and the A/B results for prompt_set_v3.

High-level summary:
- Nightly evals (2026-03-11 run) flagged a clear regression on summarization suite: R1 sim score down ~8pts (0.87 -> 0.79) compared to baseline prompt_set_v2.
- Hallucination rate (measured on fact-check subset) increased from 4.2% -> 12.5% for model variant cu_opt_q4f.
- A/B rollout (5% traffic) shows higher user-side dissatisfaction signals (CTR on suggested edits -6%, manual flag rate +2.3%).
- Changes since last stable: prompt_set_v3 introduced the new instruction framing (shorter context window + more assertive tone) and added a tiny re-rank step (heuristic scoring) - both plausible causes.

Raw numbers (from eval dashboard):
- Summarization R1 sim: baseline 0.872, v3 0.792 (delta -0.080)
- Rouge-L: baseline 0.655, v3 0.618 (delta -0.037)
- Hallucination rate (fact-check subset): baseline 4.2%, v3 12.5%
- A/B live metrics (72h): N=12k requests per cohort, flagged responses: baseline 1.9%, v3 4.2%

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Instruction framing change in prompt_set_v3 encourages brevity but causes omission of critical context -> more hallucination.
2) The heuristic re-ranker weight is over-prioritizing lexical matches and penalizing factual recall candidates.
3) Interaction with quantized kernel path for cu_opt_q4f under certain sequence lengths produces subtle tokenization differences (less likely but worth checking).

Quick checks to run before meeting (I should do these or ping owners):
- Re-run the failing evals with prompt_set_v2 vs v3 but force same decode params (temperature, top_k) to isolate prompt vs decode. (TODO: Jamie)
- Toggle re-ranker off in eval harness and re-run; compare hallucination counts. (TODO: Aisha)
- Check model runtime traces for any tokenization discrepancies around length cutoff. (TODO: infra/serving)
- Inspect a random sample (n=200) of hallucinated summaries to see pattern of omitted facts vs invented facts; tag examples for triage. (TODO: me)

Decision options to discuss in 1:1:
- Immediate rollback of A/B to prompt_set_v2 (safe, stops user regression) vs hold and iterate on v3 in a closed eval loop.
- Narrow v3 to just instruction framing change OR just re-ranker change to isolate cause.
- Increase A/B sample size and lengthen experiment window (but risk exposing more users).

Proposed immediate action (my leaning):
- Pause further rollout to 5% -> 0% (rollback) until we confirm root cause. Start two parallel fast experiments: (1) v3 without re-ranker, (2) v2 + new re-ranker to see which component drives the regression.
- Create a focused eval subset (200 examples) of high-sensitivity cases (finance/medical/legal) and run both variants there for faster signal.

Suggested agenda for the 1:1 (20 minutes):
- 0-3m: Quick recap of the regression and live impact numbers.
- 3-10m: Walk through top hypotheses and immediate checks (who does what).
- 10-16m: Decide rollback vs contained experiments and A/B sizing.
- 16-20m: Assign action items and set follow-up timing (standup + re-eval).

Notes for Aisha:
- If you think re-ranker is likely culprit, might be faster to push re-ranker-only experiment first (low engineering risk).
- If we rollback, we should include a short "what changed" blurb in the release notes to CS/Support so they can communicate with affected customers.

Action items (clear, owners, due):
- Michael: sample n=200 hallucination examples, label patterns, share doc (due: 2026-03-13).
- Aisha: run eval harness with re-ranker toggled off for v3 (due: 2026-03-13).
- Jamie: re-run prompt-only comparison with identical decode params (due: 2026-03-13).
- Samir: prepare rollback plan for A/B (how to set traffic to 0% + rollback note) and pre-draft CS blurb (due: 2026-03-12 EOD).
- Infra (ping @infra-team Slack): quick sanity check on tokenizer/sequence-length interactions for cu_opt_q4f (ask SREs) (due: 2026-03-14).

Open questions to raise:
- Do we have telemetry to correlate hallucination spikes to particular input lengths or token types?
- Can we run diff decode traces for top-k candidates pre/post re-ranker?
- Any downstream consumers that will be sensitive to a rollback (large customers on dedicated)? List owners so Samir can notify them.

Links and references:
- JIRA:EVALS-342 (regression ticket)
- Confluence: Prompt set v3 notes (link above)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/811 (re-ranker changes)

Misc notes / scratch ideas:
- If re-ranker is culprit, consider a soft-start where re-ranker weight is 0.2 -> 0.5 ramp instead of binary on/off.
- Add an automated small eval guard in the rollout pipeline: if hallucination delta > 3% on fact-check subset, fail rollout automatically.

Follow-up schedule:
- Quick sync after checks complete (slack ping) and full review in next triage (2026-03-14) if we need cross-team decisions.

-- end of prep notes --
